literal: Even though an army possesses an abundance of steadfast soldiers, in the absence of commanders, it is nothing.
translation: Even if an army has an abundance of steadfast and loyal soldiers, it will come to nothing in the absence of capable leaders.
modern: நிலைத்து நிற்கும் வீரர்களை மிகுதியாகக் கொண்டிருந்தாலும், தகுதியான தலைவர்கள் இல்லாதபோது அந்தப் படை இல்லாமல் போகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that leadership is the most critical element of a military force. Even if an army consists of a vast number of steadfast, permanent, and loyal soldiers (nilaimakkaḷ), it cannot succeed without capable commanders (talaimakkaḷ) to lead them. The term 'nilaimakkaḷ' denotes seasoned, reliable troops who do not flee, while 'talaimakkaḷ' refers to the strategic leaders. Without these leaders to guide and coordinate, the strength of the soldiers is wasted, and the army ultimately fails to exist as an effective force.
